comment: One subagent on the reply card: a panel of its own, collapsed, holding the brief it was given
and what it reported. Secondary by design — the run folds the answer into its own reply, and
this is where a reader goes to see what the work behind that reply actually was, starting with
what was asked for. The placeholders are filled in FeishuSubagentPanel: {panelId}, {bodyId} and
{footerId} are element ids, {title} says which subagent this is and how it is getting on,
{brief} is the task it was given, quoted, {body} is what it has said so far, and {footer} is
what it has spent saying it. A deployment replacing this file has to keep all six, keep the
brief first among the elements, and keep the body and footer elements text ones: the run streams
into both of them by id. The brief has no id of its own because nothing ever rewrites it alone.
The header fills the panel's width and carries its own horizontal padding, so the title reads
as a row of its own rather than as text floating beside the chevron; the chevron therefore sits
at the right edge rather than following the text. The title is notation-sized, the card's
smallest, the same size the reasoning and references panes give theirs: a closed panel is a
line offering something rather than saying it, and at body size the chevron line competes with
the answer it sits beside. The size lives on the title's markdown rather than on the panel,
because it is the header text being sized and not what the panel holds — the contents carry
their own. The chevron itself is the one the thinking
pane uses, and turns the same way: pointing right while the panel is closed and a quarter turn
down as it opens, so the two panels on a card open the same way. This key is ignored when the
panel is built.
